answer.text:
The clearest example in the archive is the remaining shelf life data field. On 18 April 2024, Tomas Lindholm asked Priya Nair whether it could be found out, saying "Can you find out?" and "Please, right because it changes the design"; Priya replied "I can ask." [1] [2] [3]

On 6 May 2024 Priya confirmed the agreement in writing: "Agreed on all four. I will own the remediation, whatever Lena says about it. On the warehouse question, I have asked. The person who owns that system is on secondment until August. I will chase in August." [4]

On 22 August 2024 Priya reported back that goods receipt date is captured but not exposed, and that getting it out means either an extract nobody owns or a change request; she wrote "I will not be raising a change request for something that is not in the current phase." Tomas Lindholm then logged it as a phase two dependency and closed the thread. [5] [6]

The question resurfaced in weekly updates through July and August 2025: on 21 July 2025 the shelf life field mapping was reported unresolved for two weeks and blocking the ordering logic; on 4 August 2025 it was still unresolved with the Acme warehouse team unavailable; on 18 August 2025 it was four weeks open and approaching the point where a workaround was needed. [7] [8] [9]

On 11 September 2025 Priya Nair wrote: "It is not impossible, it is unowned, which in practice is the same thing this year. Proceed with your approximation." The workaround was built instead of obtaining the field. [10]

At the fresh cutover call on 11 December 2025, Nadia Haddad confirmed the approximation runs but not without the warehouse data, which was first asked for in April 2024. [11] [12]

At the Q2 business review on 16 June 2026, Sofia Almeida said she spends about a day and a half out of five manually compensating on slow-moving fresh lines, because of a data field in the warehouse system first asked about in April 2024. [13] [14] [15] [16] [17] [18]

On 26 June 2026 Marco Rossi put it in writing to Robert Kahn that the twelve-month expectation was missed because "The value case depended on fresh, and fresh depended on a data field that we identified as a dependency in April 2024 and never obtained." [19]

Who would have needed to notice: Priya Nair owned the chase and stopped when the answer came back in August 2024; Tomas Lindholm logged it as a phase two dependency and closed the thread; Ana Duarte carried it in weekly status reports from July 2025 onward; and Lena Fischer said at the June 2025 steering committee that she had "never once heard it resolved." [5] [6] [7] [20] [21]

The archive shows no record of anyone escalating the shelf life field to Robert Kahn or the steering committee as a decision item before the workaround was built. Certainty is limited to the archive: it shows the agreement, the chase, the closure of the thread, and the workaround, but not every internal conversation, so it is possible someone raised it outside these records.

citations.quote:
Robert,

Indicative numbers attached. Summary here so you have it in the mail.

Chain wide for the three fresh categories, 340 stores: additional annual licence of
approximately 420 thousand, plus implementation of approximately 260 thousand one off.

On your second point, and this is the honest version.

The twelve month expectation was missed for one reason above all others. The value case
depended on fresh, and fresh depended on a data field that we identified as a dependency
in April 2024 and never obtained. Everything else largely went to plan. We built a
workaround in September 2025 which works acceptably on fast moving articles and poorly on
slow moving ones, and your category manager has been compensating for the difference by
hand ever since.

For the next number to be different, that field has to be available. It is not a RELEX
deliverable and I cannot commit to it on your behalf, which is why I am putting it in
writing rather than in a slide.

If it is not resolved, chain wide will reduce waste by less than the pilot suggests,
because the slow moving articles are a larger share of the tail across 340 stores than
across 25.
